article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu's remnants are expected to bring more rain to southern India on Thursday, while Delhi-NCR prepares for a dry day with mild temperatures and morning mist.

Amaravati: The remnants of Cyclone Murasu are expected to bring more rainfall to parts of southern India on Thursday, November 5, while Delhi-NCR is likely to experience mainly clear skies with morning mist or shallow fog.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has also forecast isolated heavy rainfall and thunderstorms in some southern and central regions.
Rainfall activity is expected to continue across several southern states as the remnants of Cyclone Murasu influence weather conditions.
The system, which crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast before weakening, has further weakened into a depression over east Telangana and adjoining coastal Andhra Pradesh.
According to the IMD, the depression is expected to move nearly northwards and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area.
However, its remaining influence is likely to bring showers to parts of southern India.
Isolated to scattered rainfall is forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Kerala, coastal Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Rayalaseema and south interior Karnataka on November 5.
Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam are also likely to receive rainfall.
The IMD has forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and south interior Karnataka.
Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are also likely over parts of coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema and south interior Karnataka.
Residents in these regions should remain alert to changing weather conditions, particularly during periods of heavy rain and thunderstorms.

stories.headline: US mid-term election outcome effect: G-Secs rally, Rupee gains
stories.title: US mid-term election outcome effect: G-Secs rally, Rupee gains
stories.summary: The Indian rupee extended its winning streak for the fourth consecutive session
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Government Securities (G-Secs) market rallied on Wednesday, tracking falling US Treasury yields and dip in crude oil prices amid the Democrats winning control of the US Congress in the mid-term elections.
The rupee too gained ground as the US dollar weakened.

Yield of the widely tracked benchmark 10-year G-Sec (6.94 per cent GS2036) dipped 12 basis points, the biggest single day decline in about six months, to close at 7.19 per cent against the previous close of 7.31 per cent.
The price of this security jumped by about 83 paise.
Yield and prices of a bond are inversely co-related and move in opposite directions.

Referring to the outcome of the US mid-term elections, Nuvama, in report, said: “For Indian government bonds, lower US yields and a weaker dollar could provide external support and improve FPI sentiment in the near term, although domestic factors and crude oil prices will remain key drivers.
For now, 10-year IGB (India Government Bond) has eased.
“But the gains on the US treasury yields may be short lived, and India yields might trade with caution over the near term, given the rally over the past few days from 7.50 per cent to 7.19 per cent.”
At the weekly Treasury Bill (T-Bill) auction, the 91-day and 364-day T-Bill auctions to mobilise ₹8,000 crore and ₹7,000 crore, sailed through.
However, the RBI rejected all bids for the 182-day T-Bill (₹8,000 crore) auction as market participants demanded higher yields.

Meanwhile, the rupee appreciated to a two-week high as the dollar weakened after the US mid-term elections showed the Democrats gaining an upper hand in the US Congress and a decline in crude oil prices.
The Indian unit closed at 94.64/65 per US dollar against the previous close of 94.74/75.

stories.headline: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners
stories.title: SC seeks Centre, EC response on law giving blanket, lifelong immunity to CEC, Election Commissioners
stories.summary: The court listed the petitions on December 18
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Union government on petitions challenging the constitutionality of a specific provision in the Chief Election Commissioner-Election Commissioners’ appointment law which grants them blanket, lifelong immunity from any legal action or criminal prosecution, not only during the official tenure but even after retirement.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notice to both the Centre and the Election Commission of India on petitions filed by RJD MP Manoj Jha, represented by Tanya Srivastava and advocate Arun Kumar Agrawal, represented by advocate Neha Rathi, challenging Section 16 of The Chief Election Commissioner And Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions Of Service And Term Of Office) Act, 2023.
The court listed the petitions on December 18.

The petitions said the Section was unconstitutional, went beyond the ambit of powers given to the Election Commission of India (EC) and, significantly, violated the Basic Structure of the Constitution.
“Section 16 of the Act bars jurisdiction of Constitutional courts and interferes with the power of judicial review, held to be a part of the Basic Structure of Constitution,” the petitions submitted.

Rathi submitted that a plain reading of the provision showed a bar on any court to entertain or continue any civil or criminal proceedings against “any person who is or was a Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner for any act, thing or word, committed, done or spoken by him when, or in the course of acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty or function”.
“A bare perusal of the text [of Section 16] discloses the width of the protection granted in so far as it bars all kinds of prosecution including corruption, forgery and other serious offences.
It provides for lifelong immunity and covers acts that may be outside lawful authority,” Agrawal’s plea contended.

Section 16 further barred proceedings instituted under defamation law, contempt law and other civil or criminal liabilities for lifetime without distinguishing between mala fide and bona fide acts, all under guise of preventing frivolous complaints against the CEC.
“The object to ensure independence by taking such sweeping measures fails the test of proportionality.
That every person has a right to a remedy and to a fair investigation, and access to justice is a facet of Articles 14 and 21,” the petitioners highlighted.
They said that until the enactment of the 2023 Act, the Parliament had not granted any blanket immunity to Election Commissioners.

stories.headline: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
stories.title: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
stories.summary: Supreme Court flags fertility decline, refers two-child rule to larger bench
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: Referring to other countries grappling with declining and ageing populations, the top court said India could not afford to ignore the changing demographic trends simply because it already had a large population.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday questioned the continued relevance of laws disqualifying people with more than two children from contesting local body elections, saying the fear of overpopulation that once justified such restrictions had weakened amid changing demographic realities.

Warning that the effects of slowing population growth could be difficult to reverse, the court stressed the need to guard against a potentially irreversible decline in fertility, news agency PTI reported.

A bench of Justices P S Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said the relevance and justification of legislation must be assessed in light of contemporary social conditions rather than solely on the circumstances prevailing when it was enacted.
"Adapting to change is important for achieving justice, as failure to adapt produces injustice and is, in a sense, an abuse of power.
Thus, failure to use power to adapt to change is in its own way an abuse of power," the bench said.

The observations came while hearing a plea by Mangala Bhimrao Ingle, whose election as sarpanch of Kakoda gram panchayat in Maharashtra was set aside on the ground that she had more than two children.
Her disqualification was based on Section 14(1)(j-1) of the Maharashtra Village Panchayats Act, 1959.
The court said a law enacted to address a particular social problem could cease to serve its intended purpose if the circumstances underlying it changed substantially.

The bench referred to the Supreme Court's July 2003 judgment in Javed vs State of Haryana, which upheld provisions of the Haryana Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, disqualifying people with more than two living children from contesting or holding panchayat positions.
It noted that India's total fertility rate (TFR) had declined from 3.0 in 2003 to 1.9, underlining the need to revisit policies framed around population control.
"The need of the hour is to have policies in tune with the present realities.

stories.headline: One Factor I Consider For Elevation Is How Judge Would Be A Team Player In Supreme Court : CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: One Factor I Consider For Elevation Is How Judge Would Be A Team Player In Supreme Court : CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: With so much filings, Supreme Court is virtually playing a T20 match, CJI said, at the SCBA felicitation for the newly elevated judges.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: With so much filings, Supreme Court is virtually playing a T20 match, CJI said, at the SCBA felicitation for the newly elevated judges.

Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Wednesday (November 4) said that one of the factors he considers while recommending judges for elevation to the Supreme Court is their ability to function as a team member, given the increasing workload and filings before the apex court.

“One of the factors which at least I have always kept in mind is how you are going to perform as a team member because Supreme Court is virtually now playing a T20 match with this much filing,” the CJI said.

He made the remarks while addressing a felicitation function organised by the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) for the newly appointed judges - Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh, who took oath on October 6.

Explaining the considerations involved in judicial appointments to the Supreme Court, CJI Surya Kant said that seniority, performance, regional representation and diversity are among the factors weighed by the Collegium.
He observed that the enormous increase in filings reflected the growing public trust in the judiciary, while also contributing to rising pendency.
The CJI also emphasised the importance of the relationship between the Bench and the Bar in the development of law.

“The bar contributes to the development of law, not merely by presenting arguments in court, but by bringing independent perspectives, rigorous research and professional insight to the court's consideration.
The bench in turn must remain open to persuasion and constructive criticism,” he said.

Describing elevation to the Supreme Court as the beginning of a different kind of responsibility, CJI Surya Kant said that the transition involved a change not merely in position but also in the scale and reach of judicial responsibility.

He commended Justice Sunita Agarwal for her administrative capabilities, particularly her work on judicial infrastructure in Gujarat, describing her as “a hardcore administrator” in addition to being a judge.
Recalling Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh's tenure as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court, the CJI referred to an old matter pending for over 10-12 years which was decided during his tenure.

The demand for tickets for the marquee clash has exceeded that of the November 21 final, which has around 79 lakh applications.
The rising demand comes despite massively skewed head-to-head figures between the nations when it comes to major ICC tournaments, where 19 of the 23 matches have been won by the Men in Blue.

stories.title: Supreme Court Upholds Rule On Pension Deduction From Salary Of Retired Govt Servants Appointed To Uttarakhand PSC

article_sentences: The Court held that the principle of 'equal pay for equal work' did not apply in the instant case.

The Supreme Court has upheld the constitutional validity of a regulation permitting the deduction of service pension from the salary payable to retired government servants appointed as Chairman or Members of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (UKPSC), holding that the pension is merely kept in abeyance during their tenure and is restored thereafter.

A bench of Justice S.V.N. Bhatti and Justice N.V. Anjaria set aside the Uttarakhand High Court's 2010 judgment which had declared Regulation 7(2) of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2004, unconstitutional for violating Article 14 read with Article 39(d) of the Constitution.
The High Court had held that deducting pension earned from previous government service from the salary payable for the constitutional post violated the principle of “equal pay for equal work.”

Disagreeing with the High Court, the Supreme Court held that the deduction did not amount to a withdrawal of the pensionary benefit, but only its temporary withholding during the period of service as Chairman or Member of the Commission.
“The question of breach of doctrine of equal pay for equal work does not arise,” the Court observed, adding that the High Court had misdirected itself in holding the regulation unconstitutional.
The Court also held that a Government servant cannot turn around to question the conditions after accepting them.

“…a Government servant or an employee, who accepts the post cannot afterwards be permitted to resile from or to agitate in respect of the service conditions and the service regulations attached to the post which he accepted.”, observed the bench.
The Respondent, having been superannuated from the Indian Army from the post of Lt. General in 2006, was appointed as Chairman of the State PSC.

Regulation 7(2) of the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Regulations, 2004 (“Regulation”), which was in force when the Respondent joined as Chairman, determines salary by applying the principle of “pay minus pension”.

This means the pension, which was entitled to be received by the Respondent upon retirement from the Indian Army, would be kept in abeyance till his current role as Chairman, and the salary for the Chairman post would exclude the pension amount.
In essence, upon appointment after retirement, the principle of “pay minus pension” was applied in determining the amount of salary.

stories.headline: TN CM Joseph Vijay Writes To PM Narendra Modi Seeking Supreme Court's Regional Bench In Chennai
stories.title: TN CM Joseph Vijay Writes To PM Narendra Modi Seeking Supreme Court's Regional Bench In Chennai
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joseph Vijay has written to the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi, reiterating the need for setting up a regional bench of the Supreme Court of India in Chennai.
In his letter, Vijay states that when the Constitution was enacted, the framers of the Constitution wanted every citizen of the country to have access to justice.

He added that presently, the remedy under Article 32 of the Constitution was available only to citizens who were geographically closer to the Supreme Court or those who were financially privileged to meet the cost of travel and litigation.

"In this connection, I would like to add that when the constitution was enacted, the framers of the constitution contemplated that all citizens of this country, rich or poor must have direct access to the Court.
It was the main reason for enactment of Article 32, a privilege not available in many other countries.

However, over the time, the remedy under Article 32 is practically available only to citizens who are geographically close to the Supreme Court of India and who are financially privileged to meet the cost of litigation and travel.
However, citizens located mainly in the South India is deprived of availing this remedy due to the sheer distance between the Southern States and New Delhi," the letter states.

Vijay pointed out that as per Article 130 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court shall sit in Delhi, or in such place of places as the Chief Justice of India may, with the approval of the President, from time to time, decide.

He pointed out that setting up of a bench of Supreme Court in Chennai, an important place in South India would benefit all the southern states, as a litigant from south will not have to travel all the way to New Delhi to get their grievance redressed.

He added that establishment of a bench at Chennai would reflect true federal character of the Nation and will not affect the independence of the judiciary since the control over the bench would remain with the Chief Justice of India.

He also stated that the Madras High Court, one of the oldest chartered High Courts in India, had a highly professional, talented, and competent bar which would meet the proposed need of the Supreme Court bench at Chennai.

He further added that despite the State's assurance that it would provide the necessary infrastructure facilities, including residential accommodation for the Supreme Court Judges befitting their status, etc., the full court of the Supreme Court, in its meeting on August 7, 2007, had refused to reconsider its earlier decision against setting up a bench.

stories.headline: Iran exempts ships from India and 3 other nations from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz
stories.title: Iran exempts ships from India and 3 other nations from transit restrictions in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Dubai, Nov 4: Iran has exempted commercial ships from four countries, including India and China, from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz, a top Iranian official has said, amid continued attacks on vessels attempting to cross the strategic waterway. Amir Hayat Moghadam, Deputy Chairman of the Iranian Parliament's National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, made the announcement in an interview with the Iranian Students' News Agency (ISNA) on Tuesday. "We have currently exempted four countries - India, China, Iraq and Qatar - from transit restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either," he was quoted as saying by the semi-official news agency. Moqaddam said the exemptions were based on specific considerations and mutual interests. He said that facilitating the passage of Indian ships was intended to allow imports of medicines from India, while the exemption for Chinese vessels was intended to secure Beijing's political support. The Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman, handles roughly 20 per cent of global energy supplies in normal times. Shipping through the waterway has been severely disrupted since February 28, when the US and Israel launched joint attacks on Iran, triggering retaliatory strikes. Iran moved to shut the waterway soon after the US-Israeli bombing began, and Washington responded weeks later with a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Iran, which has imposed strict restrictions on traffic, allows only a few vessels to pass through the waterway while others undergo screening and, in some cases, pay transit fees. At least 15 Indian seafarers have been killed in attacks on ships in the region since the conflict began in February. In the latest incident, an Indian sailor was killed in an attack on the commercial vessel MSV Al Jusufi near Limah in Oman on Monday evening. India, which has been consistently calling for finding a solution to the conflict through dialogue and diplomacy, has termed the continuing incidents of attacks on commercial shipping in the region as "deeply concerning". India has said that the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest.

stories.headline: US sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over Iran ties
stories.title: US sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over Iran ties
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The sanctions are part of the Trump administration's "Operation Economic Outcast," which aims to cut off Iran's ability to sell oil to fund the war with the US and Israel.

Treasury unveiled the new sanctions a day after Democrats made huge gains in midterm elections, winning control of both houses of Congress as voters expressed anger about the Iran war and its impact in fueling US inflation.
Treasury last week said its actions were decimating Iran's economy, driving the rial currency to new lows and sending domestic inflation rates to levels around 90%.

Treasury said Wednesday's action targeted what it called "the vast criminal network" run by India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma, his wife Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, and two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, as well as nine separate entities connected to Sharma.

"Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement.
False flags and fake maritime certifications allow vessels engaging in illicit activity to evade international safety and environmental regulations, carrying no indemnity insurance.
That means such vessels could potentially cause billions of dollars in damages to the economies of the countries in whose territorial waters they operate.
The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the US government would continue to go after anyone who supported Tehran.
"We know where you are, and we will sanction those who continue supporting the Iranian regime, whether by land, sea, or air," he said in a statement.
Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control also issued a new alert to industry, warning of the sanctions risk of dealing with potentially false flagged vessels.

It said Sharma and Shahid, based in Chandigarh, India, had fraudulently claimed to represent countries like Guyana, Eswatini and Laos in issuing flags and certifications, allowing vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies to evade international restrictions and keep operating.

stories.headline: Div Com Kashmir reviews progress of Jhelum Water Transport Project
stories.title: Div Com Kashmir reviews progress of Jhelum Water Transport Project
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 4: Divisional Commissioner Kashmir, Anshul Garg, on Wednesday chaired a high-level meeting to review the progress made in resolving various issues and bottlenecks affecting the progress of water transport facilities along River Jhelum. The meeting was convened to assess the status of issues faced by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) project and to ensure coordinated efforts among the concerned departments for facilitating the smooth execution and timely advancement of the Jhelum Water Transport Project. The meeting was attended by the Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC), Deputy Commissioners of Srinagar and Bandipora, Regional Transport Officer (RTO) Kashmir, representatives of the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), and officers from the Public Health Engineering (PHE), Irrigation and Flood Control (I&FC), Urban Environmental Engineering Department (UEED) and other concerned departments. During the meeting, the Divisional Commissioner undertook a detailed review of the progress on several critical issues requiring inter-departmental coordination and timely intervention. The matters discussed included road widening and removal of trees at Gund Parang, disposal of treated wastewater, and installation of electricity connections and provision of water supply at eight identified locations to facilitate the development of essential infrastructure for water transport operations. He also reviewed the status of shifting electrical utilities at Maharaj Gunj and Pantha Chowk, emphasising the need for expediting the process to avoid any further delays in the execution of project-related works. The meeting further deliberated on the development and improvement of approach roads at Sumbal and Sangam, removal of barricading at Amira Kadal, and shifting of houseboats wherever required to facilitate the smooth movement and operation of water transport facilities along the river. Other important issues reviewed during the meeting included renovation of the Chattabal Navigational Lock, besides relocation of stone-chiselling units and dress vendors operating at Pantha Chowk to ensure that these activities do not impede the progress of the project. Taking stock of the progress achieved so far, the Divisional Commissioner issued a series of directions to the concerned departments, asking them to take necessary measures and resolve the pending issues on priority. He stressed the importance of close coordination among all stakeholder departments and called for a result-oriented approach to address the identified bottlenecks within the shortest possible time. The Divisional Commissioner underscored that the Jhelum Water Transport Project is being closely monitored by the Government of India and, therefore, all concerned departments must demonstrate urgency and ommitment in completing the requisite preparatory works. He impressed upon the officers to accelerate the pace of work, expedite the shifting of utilities and ensure timely resolution of all pending issues so that the project can move forward without unnecessary delays.
